## 1. Build build a baseline before a bigger model

Use sklearn.datasets.load_iris and train_test_split with test_size=0.25, random_state=42, stratify=y. Fit DummyClassifier(strategy="most_frequent") and DecisionTreeClassifier(max_depth=3, random_state=42) using training data only. Report test size, accuracy, and confusion matrix for each; explain matrix rows and columns.

Predict an ordinary result before coding. Start with the smallest part you can
run and inspect. Use Colab for notebooks and the local workspace introduced in
the units for packaging or command-line tasks.

## 2. Set up the experiment

```python
from sklearn.datasets import load_iris
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split

X, y = load_iris(return_X_y=True)
X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test = train_test_split(
    X, y, test_size=0.25, random_state=42, stratify=y
)
# Fit both estimators on training data only.
```

The starter is deliberately incomplete. Implement the contract; do not change
the expected results to match an incorrect implementation.

## 3. Check the observable results

1. There are 112 training examples and 38 test examples, with all three classes in each.
2. Each confusion matrix sums to 38; trace divided by 38 agrees with accuracy.
3. The baseline predicts only its learned majority class; explain what the comparison tests.
4. Record scikit-learn version, seed, parameters, and metrics; do not require exact accuracy across versions.

Record actual outputs beside predictions. Reduce a failure to a small example,
change one cause at a time, and repeat the failed check after repairing it.

## 4. Change one condition

Try a deeper tree using a validation partition within the training set. Choose depth there, then evaluate once on the held-out test set. Explain why repeated test-driven choices would compromise the test.
